trust_decision.summary: For a request, AccessControlDomainMatcher.IsMatch decides whether the target hostname falls under an access-control rule; rules are evaluated first-match-wins and a non-matching specific rule lets a broader rule (or the default policy) decide the required authentication level.

landing_point.why: The summary 'Access Control Rule Mismatch' plus the diff's three changed lines point straight at IsMatch's wildcard branches, so an engineer looks at the *. / {user} / {group} suffix comparisons first.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP authorization endpoints registered per Authz implementation: /api/authz/legacy, /api/authz/forward-auth, /api/authz/ext-authz, /api/authz/auth-request (internal/server/handlers.go:229-252) and the CLI 'authelia access-control check-policy' (internal/commands/acl.go:225)

fix_sites.where: fix.diff:161-163 (new StringHasSuffixFold added at the end of internal/utils/strings.go)
fix_sites.entry_point: shared string helper; only reachable through the matcher above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The utils site is the project's other hostname-suffix matcher and it serves session-cookie provider selection, redirect-target validation and config validation, not the ACL; the advisory and the diff are about access-control rules, and a mismatch there fails closed (400 / rejected redirect), so an engineer can plausibly leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The {user} branch compares the sub-label against subject.Username exactly and enforces len(domain) > len(m.Name), mirroring the case-sensitive 'user:' subject rules; lowercasing the request domain once (in NewObject or at the top of IsMatch) would break {user} rules for mixed-case usernames, and a naive fold without the length guard would make the exact host '-user.domain.com' match a {user}.domain.com rule.

O6_input_shapes: plain (non-wildcard) domain rule: already compared with strings.EqualFold, unchanged by the fix (internal/authorization/access_control_domain.go:82)
'*.' suffix wildcard with mixed-case host labels (line 66)
'{user}.' suffix wildcard with mixed-case host labels, anonymous subject (line 68)
'{group}.' suffix wildcard with mixed-case host labels, anonymous subject (line 74)

mixed case must stay confined to labels above the configured session root domain, otherwise the case-sensitive session lookup rejects the request (internal/middlewares/authelia_context.go:259 via internal/utils/url.go:66)
exact host equal in length to the wildcard name must still not match ({user}/{group} length guard kept at lines 69 and 75)

O7_producer.where: internal/authorization/types.go:90-97 (NewObject sets Object.Domain = targetURL.Hostname() with no case normalization)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Authenticated ({user}. / {group}.) domain rules still compare the request domain case-sensitively: line 72 uses 'domain == username+name' and line 80 uses 'domain[i:] == m.Name', so a mixed-case host skips the specific rule and falls through to a broader bypass rule.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report and the published fix only show '*. ' wildcard rules; dynamic-subject rules are a different syntax, {user}. is documented as deprecated, and usernames are case-sensitive identity values, so the report can be read as not covering them.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, lines 72 and 80 - 0 files, 0 packages

O8_uncovered_routes.route: domain_regex rules are matched with regexp.MatchString and stay case-sensitive, so a mixed-case host skips a regex rule and falls through to the next matching rule.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Regex criteria are raw user-authored patterns where case sensitivity is the author's choice, so the advisory's case-insensitivity property arguably does not apply; docs only promise case-insensitivity for named regex groups.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file - 1 file, 0 packages

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a case-insensitive variant of HasDomainSuffix used by a session/provider or redirect-safety check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project keeps its domain-suffix primitive here and the fix added a fold helper to the same package (internal/utils/strings.go), so a maintainer could plausibly have written the fold version alongside it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second host-to-configuration lookup (another provider resolved from the request hostname)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GetCookieDomainFromTargetURI already maps a request hostname to configuration; adding a parallel lookup for another provider naturally copies the same suffix test.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third rule syntax parsed in NewAccessControlDomain and matched in the same IsMatch switch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NewAccessControlDomain already dispatches per syntax prefix (*., {user}., {group}.), so a new prefix is an ordinary maintainer change that lands in this function.

O9_family: authorization bypass via incorrect handling of case sensitivity (CWE-178, CWE-863)

TestShouldCheckDomainMatching / domain-regex tests (authorizer_test.go), access_control_rule_test.go, types_test.go; also internal/handlers authz-implementation tests and internal/commands/acl_test.go

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap only the three strings.HasSuffix calls for a case-insensitive helper (or lowercase the domain once in NewObject/IsMatch), which leaves the authenticated {user}/{group} comparisons exact and breaks mixed-case usernames.

out_of_scope_notes: The same case-sensitive suffix primitive also backs fail-closed checks (session cookie domain selection and redirect-target validation); noted only as the O2/O3 site, not pursued.
